page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8269CY x86_64 processor running at 2.5 GHz, with 1 thread per core. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates a clear contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, such as stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the weak and poor categories, representing the bottom 10% to 25% of tested hardware. However, multi-core performance is consistently average, as demonstrated by the Geekbench multi-core score of 5755.0 and Passmark CPU score of 13059.36. Memory bandwidth tests show average read and write speeds, though the Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory density and average multi-core processing capabilities, this instance is suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high single-thread performance. Appropriate applications include Redis in-memory databases, which achieved an average of 11.3 million operations per second in testing, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression tasks. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1.4xlarge offers a high-capacity memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads requiring large memory footprints without the premium cost of high-frequency compute cores.
